sources.citation: Chen, Litong. 2012. Shaoguan Tuhua, a Local Vernacular of Northern Guangdong Province, China: A New Look from a Quantitative and Contact Linguistic Perspective. MA thesis, Ohio State University (OhioLINK osu1342628552), 187 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Quantitative/contact study reanalysing Li & Zhuang 2009 data; no phonology chapter; only second-hand tone-value notes (e.g. 'The tone value of the Shang tone in Shibei Shaoguan Tuhua is 24 (Li and Zhuang 2009:93, 18)'). a full-text search for stress/accent/neutral tone: no hits except 'accent' in the sense of regional accent.

sources.citation: Cheng, Ming-chung. 2010. The geographic distribution of the diminutives in Yuebei Tuhua: a compromise of the conflict between two forces of diminutive formation in southeastern Chinese dialects. Concentric: Studies in Linguistics 36.2: 213-233.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; treats diminutive tone change and glottal-stop insertion across Yuebei Tuhua points (Shaoguan, Qujiang: Baisha, Zhoutian etc.) using Zhuang 2004 data.

sources.citation: Cheng, Ming-chung. 2009. The diachronic change of the diminutives in Yuebei Tuhua: an Optimality-Theoretical analysis with partially ordered constraints. Concentric: Studies in Linguistics 35.2: 245-267.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; 'prosodic' appears only in OT constraint terminology.
